prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively name a single “best” attorney for every person or case — the right lawyer depends on the specifics of your crash, injuries, insurance coverages, and whether you’ll likely need a trial. I can, however, help you find a top attorney for your situation and give a practical checklist so you can choose with confidence.

If you want a quick next step, tell me your ZIP code and a few facts about the crash (date, injuries, dispute with an insurer, whether the other driver was uninsured/underinsured, any hospital stays), and I’ll suggest several highly qualified Chicago attorneys/firms to contact.

How to find the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car-accident claim
1. Look for relevant experience
 - Focus on attorneys who handle car-accident and motor-vehicle injury cases every day (not general practitioners).
 - Prefer lawyers with significant trial experience if your case may go to court.

2. Check qualifications and recognition
 - Peer-review ratings (Martindale-Hubbell AV-rated), Super Lawyers, Million Dollar Advocates, and local Plaintiffs’ bar groups (e.g., Illinois Trial Lawyers Association).
 - Board certification is rare in PI, but any additional credentials, law review work, or teaching/lecturing on auto-injury topics are good signs.

3. Verify results and client satisfaction
 - Ask about verdicts/settlements in cases similar to yours (severity, liability issues).
 - Read client reviews on multiple sites (Google, Yelp, Avvo/Super Lawyers profiles), but weigh them with caution.

4. Confirm they handle contingency-fee cases
 - Most PI attorneys work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Confirm the percentage, who advances costs, and what expenses you may owe if you don’t win.

5. Check disciplinary history
 - Look up the attorney with the Illinois Attorney Registration & Disciplinary Commission (ARDC) to confirm there are no ethics problems.

Questions to ask in a free consultation
 - Have you handled cases like mine? What were the outcomes?
 - Who will handle my case day‑to‑day (attorney vs. paralegal)?
 - What is your trial experience? Have you taken cases to jury verdicts recently?
 - How do you charge? What percentage and what costs are deducted from recovery?
 - How long do you expect my case to take?
 - How will you keep me informed about progress?
 - Can you provide client references or examples of similar cases?

Red flags
 - Guarantees of a specific settlement figure.
 - Requests for large up‑front retainers (beyond typical case costs).
 - Unwillingness to put fee agreements in writing.
 - Poor or evasive communication during the consultation.
 - No courtroom experience if liability or damages are contested.

Where to search and verify attorneys
 - SuperLawyers.com (Illinois/Chicago lists)
 - Martindale‑Hubbell peer-review ratings
 - Avvo and Google/Yelp for client reviews
 - Illinois Trial Lawyers Association or local trial lawyer groups
 - Illinois ARDC for disciplinary records

If you’d like, give me:
 - Your ZIP code (or neighborhood)
 - A short summary of the crash and injuries
I’ll pull together 3–5 Chicago personal injury attorneys/firms who are well-suited to your case and explain why each might be a good fit.
